summary: kmf-bootstrap postinstall exfiltrates installer identifiers to hardcoded C2 via DNS and HTTP
details: On npm install, kmf-bootstrap@100.100.103 executes a postinstall script that encodes the installer's hostname and the package name as a subdomain of db4jlbku53082dmp0d7g3mffj7s7aordk.oast.me and triggers a DNS resolution against that interactsh collector. It then requires a bundled native addon (prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node, an ELF Node-API module) which forks and opens a socket to the hardcoded IP 64.181.165.115 on port 80, sending `POST /dc HTTP/1.0` with form fields `h`, `u`, `p`, `r` populated from gethostname, getpwuid/getenv, the package name, and the configured npm registry URL. If the native addon fails to load, the JS falls back to the same HTTP POST to 64.181.165.115/dc using Node's http module. Both the `http` module name and the destination IP are reconstructed at runtime from character and integer arrays (`['h','t','t','p'].join('')`, `[64,181,165,115].join('.')`) rather than appearing as string literals, and the primary exfiltration path is hidden inside the compiled addon. The destinations are not associated with any declared purpose of the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
